newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela saved $1.6 bln of oil windfall - Giusti.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela saved $1.6 bln of oil windfall - Giusti.

text.p: The Venezuelan government has so far saved some 750 billion bolivars ($1.6 billion) of last year's windfall oil revenues and placed them in a special account, PdVSA president Luis Giusti said.
"The government has so far put 750 billion bolivars into the account," Giusti said at a seminar on the Venezuelan economy hosted by the Venezuelan-American Chamber of Commerce.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, 80 percent of petro-dollars gained from oil prices above $14.70 a barrel in 1996 were due to be placed in a special account with the Treasury. The account was earmarked to be used to set up a macroeconomic stabilization fund or to pay off international debt.
Last year the average export price for Venezuela's basket of oil crudes and products averaged $18.25 per barrel. On Friday, the average export price fell by $1.26 to $21.24.
